user_stories.story: As the maintainer, I want one parent API router carrying the key check, so a new /api router added to it is protected without remembering a per-include flag.
As the maintainer, I want a test that fails when any /api route lacks the key check, so a router included outside the parent cannot ship unnoticed.
As an API client or the dashboard, I want every URL, method, status code, 401 body, and the open /health, docs, CORS preflight and /ws behaviour unchanged.

arrangement.current: Each child router already declares its FULL path prefix: alerts = APIRouter(prefix="/api/alerts"), rules = APIRouter(prefix="/api/rules"), symbols = APIRouter(prefix="/api/symbols"); route decorators use "" or "/{rule_id}". health and ws have no /api prefix and are not under the parent.
arrangement.decision: The parent router has NO prefix (empty) and carries dependencies=[Depends(require_api_key)]. The three child routers are included into it with no prefix argument and are NOT edited. Final path = child prefix + route path, exactly as today (e.g. /api/rules + "/{rule_id}"). The app includes only the parent (replacing the three include_router(..., dependencies=auth) lines and the `auth` list). health.router and ws.router stay included directly on the app, unchanged. Rejected alternative: parent prefix="/api" plus shortening child prefixes to "/rules" etc. It edits three more files for no gain and risks double "/api".
arrangement.placement: The parent is built fresh inside create_app (or a small helper called by it), not as a module-level object. Reason: include_router copies routes, so a shared module-level parent would accumulate duplicate routes on every create_app call (tests call create_app many times). A short comment at the parent says: add every future /api router here; /health and /ws are deliberately outside.
arrangement.dependency_inheritance: Dependencies added at parent level are prepended to each route's dependant tree, so the check still runs before body validation (401 not 422), as today.

route_walk_test.location: New file backend/tests/test_api_auth_coverage.py (no edits to test_auth.py or any existing assertion). Uses existing fixtures/helpers (settings, fake_db, FakeFinnhubClient, create_app); never touches the network or Postgres.
route_walk_test.walker: A helper function (in the test file) takes a FastAPI app and returns the list of offending routes. It iterates app.routes; for every route whose path == "/api" or starts with "/api/", it recursively traverses route.dependant.dependencies (each sub-dependant's .call and its own .dependencies) and requires that some dependant's .call is the require_api_key function object (identity check imported from app.security). Source text and dependency names are not inspected. Applies to APIRoute and websocket routes with a dependant; any /api route without a dependant (e.g. a Mount) counts as an offender.

tests.test: Real app: walker returns [] for create_app(...) and the number of /api routes inspected is greater than 0 (guards against a vacuous pass); the inspected set includes at least /api/rules, /api/rules/{rule_id}, /api/alerts, /api/symbols.

Self-check (proves detection inside the test, no production edit): build a real app via create_app, then app.include_router(dummy) where dummy = APIRouter(prefix="/api/x") with a trivial GET "" handler and no dependencies; assert walker returns exactly that route (path "/api/x"). Also assert a second variant: a dummy router included with a dependency that is not require_api_key (e.g. a no-op dependency) is still flagged. Optionally a positive control: dummy included with dependencies=[Depends(require_api_key)] is not flagged, confirming the walker accepts a legitimately protected route.
Open routes are not mistaken for offenders: /health, /openapi.json, /docs, /redoc, /ws are not walked (they do not start with /api).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: create_app includes exactly one API parent router carrying Depends(require_api_key); symbols, rules and alerts routers are included into it and none of the three is included directly on the app. How to test: inspect app.routes in the walker test (criterion 3) and review the diff of main.py; grep main.py shows no include_router call for symbols/rules/alerts on `app`.

Every existing URL, method and status code is unchanged, and OpenAPI paths are identical. How to test: BEFORE editing production code, dump json.dumps(create_app(test settings, FakeFinnhubClient.factory, FakeDatabase()).openapi(), sort_keys=True) and the sorted list of (path, sorted methods) for all app.routes to a scratchpad file outside the repo; AFTER the change dump again and diff: the two must be byte-identical (no security scheme is added because require_api_key takes only Request). Existing suite passes with no assertion edits.

The route-walk test passes on the real app and fails (walker non-empty) for any /api route lacking require_api_key in its dependant tree. How to test: run the new test file; the real-app test reports a positive count of inspected routes.

Self-check: after including a dummy unprotected /api/x router directly on a created app, the walker returns that route; a dummy with a non-key dependency is also flagged. How to test: the self-check tests in the new file pass.

401 {"detail": "invalid or missing API key"} for missing, empty, wrong and non-ASCII key on all /api routes, and an invalid body without a key still yields 401 not 422. How to test: existing test_auth.py (unchanged) passes.

/health, /docs, /redoc, /openapi.json answer 200 without a key; CORS preflight OPTIONS /api/rules without a key returns 200 with the allow-origin and allow-headers. How to test: existing test_health_open and test_preflight_without_key pass; add (in the new file) a quick unauthenticated GET check for /docs, /redoc, /openapi.json returning 200.
/ws keeps its own Origin plus ?key= check and is not under the parent router. How to test: existing ws tests in test_auth.py pass; walker test confirms /ws is not walked.
Repeated create_app calls do not duplicate routes. How to test: in the new file, create two apps in one process and assert each has the same number of /api routes as the first.

Offline `python -X faulthandler -m pytest -o faulthandler_timeout=120` passes; the real-Postgres run on the throwaway PG17 cluster (port 55521, trust auth, temp dir outside repo) passes with 0 skipped, then the cluster is stopped and deleted and no process the agent started remains.

assumptions.assumption: Parent router is unprefixed because the children already carry full /api prefixes (resolution of the "full paths vs prefixes" question; child files untouched).
"Starts with /api" is implemented as path == "/api" or startswith("/api/"), to avoid flagging an unrelated future path like /apiary while covering all real API paths.
The parent is built inside create_app rather than at module level (avoids route accumulation across repeated create_app calls); the "single obvious place" is a clearly commented block in create_app.
The one-line CLAUDE.md note is written by the orchestrator, not the implementer.
The before/after OpenAPI snapshot is a one-off verification kept in the scratchpad, not a committed test (no new fixture files in the repo).

edge_cases.case: Route with parameter path (/api/rules/{rule_id}): matched by its template string; walker must handle it.
Dependency nested deeper than one level (a route dependency that itself depends on require_api_key): walker must recurse, so it counts as protected.

Router included outside the parent with its own dependencies=[Depends(require_api_key)]: it is protected, so the walker does not flag it (the guarantee is "carries the check", not "included in the parent"). The self-check for "outside the parent" uses an unprotected dummy.
Empty-string route paths ("") under a prefix resolve to /api/alerts etc. with no trailing-slash redirect change.
Starlette mounts under /api expose no dependant: flagged as offenders.

ambiguities.item: The request says the test must fail "when a router is included outside the parent". Strictly, a router included outside the parent but with its own key dependency is still safe. Resolution: the walker enforces the security property (key in the dependant tree), which is what makes unprotected outside-the-parent includes fail; the self-check demonstrates this with an unprotected dummy.
Where "the parent" lives (main.py vs a new routers/api.py). Resolution: inside main.py's create_app, to keep changes minimal (no new production files).

risks.risk: Duplicate-route accumulation if the parent were module-level; mitigated by building it per create_app and criterion 8.
Route ordering or OpenAPI operation order could differ after re-nesting; mitigated by the byte-identical OpenAPI diff in criterion 2.

Walker could pass vacuously (zero /api routes inspected or wrong attribute on a FastAPI/Starlette version); mitigated by the positive-count assertion and the self-check that must flag a known-bad route.

spec.dependencies: backend/app/main.py (only production file changed), backend/app/security.py (require_api_key, imported by identity in the test), backend/app/routers/{alerts,rules,symbols}.py (read-only), backend/tests/conftest.py fixtures, tests/fakes/fake_db.py and fake_finnhub.py, FastAPI/Starlette already pinned in requirements.txt.
spec.out_of_scope: Any other medium items; websocket changes (/ws gate stays as is); new endpoints; changing child router prefixes or route handlers; changing the 401 body or require_api_key logic; auth for /health, docs or CORS; docs other than the orchestrator's one-line CLAUDE.md note; any git or gh command, commits, stash, checkout, restore (hard constraint); printing .env values.
spec.self_critique: Every story maps to criteria: parent router (1, 8), detection test (3, 4), unchanged behaviour (2, 5, 6, 7, 9). All criteria are observable by pytest or a diff. Biggest remaining risk: the walker's dependant traversal depends on FastAPI internals (route.dependant.dependencies, .call), so a FastAPI upgrade could silently change it; the positive-count and self-check tests guard against that. Secondary: the baseline OpenAPI dump must be captured before the first production edit, or criterion 2 cannot be verified.
